title: Risk-weighted Intake Conductor: Automated Evidence Bundles and SLA Negotiation for Cross-border Data Requests
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Background: Enterprise customers frequently submit security and compliance questionnaires, DPA exception requests, and region-specific data residency asks. Today these are triaged manually across PM, Legal, Security, and Solutions teams which causes inconsistent SLAs, duplicated evidence requests, and slow time-to-contract. Goal: build a 'Risk-weighted Intake Conductor' -- an automated intake layer that assigns a risk score to incoming security/compliance requests, auto-assembles a prioritized evidence bundle, and surfaces tailored SLA negotiation guidance (including escalation to Legal for DPR/DPA exceptions).

Scope: PoC will cover written questionnaires, DPA exception forms, and vendor security surveys for SOC2/ISO, GDPR/DPA, and HIPAA-related asks. Out of scope for Phase 1: full legal contract revisions, on-prem deployment for customer-managed infra, and automated legal-signature workflows.

Success metrics: reduce mean time to first-response for high-risk asks from 5 business days to 24 hours; increase fraction of requests that are fully evidence-complete on first reply from ~18% to >65%; reduce Legal handoff volume by 40% through decision heuristics and templated responses.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming request is assigned a reproducible risk score based on source, data classification, and contractual ask
System generates an evidence bundle with links to stored artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption diagrams, data flow maps) and an evidence completeness score
Automatic SLA recommendation generated (e.g., 72h standard, 24h expedited) with justification and escalation path
Triage UI exposes a one-click 'send evidence bundle' reply and a 'request more info' template to reduce back-and-forth
Legal escalation only triggered when heuristics indicate true contract or data-residency exception with a clear audit trail
tasks: Draft PRD and decision-graph (owner: PM) - include DPAs, country/residency rules and control mappings
Map existing evidence artifacts and canonical storage locations (owner: Security) - where SOC2 reports, penetration test reports, and encryption keys manifests live
Prototype scoring heuristic (owner: Applied ML) - small model + rules engine for risk score
Design triage UI wireframes and one-click reply flow (owner: Design)
Implement backend endpoints for bundle generation and templated replies (owner: ENG)
Integrate with ticketing (Zendesk/Front) and internal Slack channel for escalations
Legal review of SLA templates and escalation criteria (owner: Legal)
Pilot with 5 strategic customers and collect feedback
comments: 2026-03-02 - Anjali Rao: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Agreement to prioritize cross-border DPAs first due to several active sales deals in EMEA. Action: Security to provide list of canonical evidence artifacts by 2026-03-09.

2026-03-04 - Marcus Lee: Met with Applied ML. Proposed hybrid approach: rule-based filters for high precision + lightweight risk classifier to rank medium-risk items. ML to produce confidence score; low-confidence routed to human triage.

2026-03-05 - Priya Sharma (Security): Listed storage locations for SOC2 report, pen-test summary, and KMS proof in the corporate Drive. Note: encryption key manifests live in Vault and require role-based access to include in bundles (need eng support).

2026-03-06 - Legal (Evan Ortiz): Reviewed draft SLA tiers. Recommend adding 'Data Residency Conditional' clause for APAC customers; require Legal approval for any DPA override. Also suggest a conservative default time-to-respond for HIPAA-related asks.

2026-03-08 - Marcus Lee: Decided to scope Phase 1 to read-only evidence bundles (links + redacted artifacts) rather than attaching raw documents to outbound replies. This avoids additional access controls for now and accelerates delivery.
notes: Trade-offs considered: a fully automated contract editing flow would be higher ROI long-term but increases legal risk and implementation time; we prefer an evidence-first approach for Phase 1.
Privacy constraint: evidence bundle generation must not expose PII nor raw customer data. Attachments should be redacted or replaced with canonical proof artifacts.
Operational constraint: any automatic reply must include audit metadata (who/what/when) for SOC/ISO traceability.
Escalation matrix draft: PM -> Security -> Legal -> CTO for emergency overrides
customer_stories: As an enterprise procurement lead I want one authoritative response that includes all required artifacts so I can complete the vendor security review within the first interaction.
As a Solutions Engineer I want an evidence bundle I can send directly to customers that maps questionnaire items to supporting artifacts so I avoid repetitive manual searches.
